The journalist and filmmaker hardly sleeps anymore and has only one thing on his mind: saving his family and showing the daily reality of besieged Palestinians.
Avant les bombardements actuels sur la b: Before the current bombing of the Gaza Strip, Ibrahim was a fixer, that is, a journalist for foreign journalists who come to cover stories from the enclave, and a filmmaker. Since October 7, he has been informing the world about daily life in Gaza on his social media accounts.
« Ce qui nous rend heureux, lorsque nous: “What makes us happy, when we are lucky enough to get an Internet connection back, is seeing that people are protesting, talking about what is happening in Gaza. We feel understood,” he says, even though he is largely disappointed by international media coverage.
« J’ai fait un <em>live</em> avec des mé: “I did a live with media outlets that didn’t believe me,” he says. “Sometimes we feel like we don’t live in the same world or on the same planet.”
« Ce sont vraiment les réseaux sociaux q: “It’s really social media that saves us,” believes Ibrahim. As soon as he gets Internet back, he bears witness, reporting mainly that all people do is share videos or information about the situation with their loved ones or on their own accounts.

« Ce qui me rend triste, c’est de penser: “What makes me sad is thinking about my home, about life before, and comparing it to now,” says Ibrahim, tears in his eyes. Planes fly over us all night, the bombing never stops, and you tell yourself that any minute now something is going to happen,” the filmmaker recounts. “We don’t have a pillow, anyway, it’s not comfortable at all.”
Occupé toute la journée à filmer, il se: Busy filming all day, he tells himself he will manage to sleep. But it’s impossible to close his eyes. “My friends saw me online, and I told them: ‘I’m traumatized, I heard on the news that there might be an invasion of Rafah, and I wonder where I should go, how I’m going to protect my family…’ My mother needs dialysis three times a week… What am I going to do?” he says.

Ibrahim has never seen anything like this: “If you ask people here, everyone wants to leave. [...] Normally, no Palestinian wants to leave their land, but after what we have seen, no one wants to stay here anymore.”

He is deeply anxious, especially when he sees young people completely traumatized by the situation. This is the case of a little girl who had a leg amputated, whom he wanted to speak to and who refused to speak to anyone.
« Cela fait deux mois qu’elle refuse de: “It’s been two months since she’s refused to speak. We tried giving her toys, food, she doesn’t speak,” he says in despair.

The boy from northern Gaza had to have a limb amputated at the American hospital in Gaza. Several people are organizing so that he can be evacuated from the Gaza Strip as a priority in order to get a prosthesis. “We promise him he’ll have Spiderman’s leg, that he’ll be the next Spiderman,” says Ibrahim, referring to the spider-powered superhero.

He asks: “Can you imagine that for four months these children have been caught in the middle of this war, facing famine and no longer going to school?”

Sa fille de quatre ans a déjà vécu deux: His four-year-old daughter has already lived through two wars. “What kind of future am I giving her if we stay in Gaza?” he says in an interview with La Converse. “There’s no school, no mosque, no hope.”

« Nous empruntons de l’argent à gauche e: “We borrow money left and right, and people are starting to turn into thieves. They have no choice, they’re starving,” he says. “If we don’t die from the war, we’re going to die of hunger.”
